content:
**Jev** (current version `jev-1.13.0`, aliases `jev-latest` / `jev-preview`) is TypeSafe.ai’s flagship “System One” model. It is optimized for fast, structured decisions (Choice, Score, or Noul primitives with probabilities and confidence) rather than text generation. It takes a `state` (text, JSON object, or array) plus multiple typed questions in one call and returns machine-readable outputs. Input is text/structured data only.[[1]](https://docs.typesafe.ai/models)

### Pricing
- **Input tokens**: $0.042 per million tokens (**$42 per billion tokens** / Btok).[[1]](https://docs.typesafe.ai/models)
- **Output tokens**: Free (“too cheap to meter”).
- You are charged only for input tokens sent in each request. Output and small fixed-shape answers are not billed. Batching multiple questions in one request (they share the state) is the main way to reduce cost and latency.[[2]](https://opentweet.io/jev/limits)

There is **no documented server-side prompt/cached tokens discount** or separate cached-tokens rate. “Caching” in the documentation and cookbooks refers to **client-side JSON caches** used in notebooks and examples so repeated runs replay stored results instead of hitting the API (for development and reproducible benchmarks). No prepaid tiers, free allowance, or volume discounts are published in the core docs (some third-party sites mention prepaid credits or small new-account credits, but official sources emphasize straightforward per-input-token billing).[[3]](https://jevaiguide.com/jev-pricing/)

Enterprise/custom plans exist for high volume; contact sales@typesafe.ai. Pricing and limits can change.

### Rate Limits (per account)
Current documented limits (as of mid-October 2026 docs):

- **100K tokens per second**
- **80 requests per second**

Exceeding either returns **HTTP 429 Too Many Requests**. SDKs automatically retry with exponential backoff and respect the `retry-after` header. There is also a **529 Overloaded** status for temporary platform issues.[[4]](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api)

**Important notes**:
- Limits are **adjusting dynamically** due to high demand and can change without notice as capacity expands.
- Earlier launch figures were different (e.g., 250K tokens/s and 1,200 requests/minute); always check the live models page.
- Higher limits are available on custom and enterprise plans. Contact sales@typesafe.ai for teams or high-volume use.[[1]](https://docs.typesafe.ai/models)

**Context window**: 64k tokens per request total; 32k tokens budget for the state plus the single longest question. Accuracy can vary as state size grows.

### API Keys and Authentication
- Create and manage keys in the **TypeSafe console** (typically console.typesafe.ai/keys or linked from the quickstart).
- Use the standard header: `Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>`.
- The official Python (`typesafe-sdk`) and JavaScript/TypeScript SDKs read the `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` environment variable by default and handle retries, connection reuse, etc.
- Endpoint: `POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone` (with JSON body containing `model`, `state`, and `questions` map). Responses include `usage` with `input_tokens` and `output_tokens`.[[5]](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction/quickstart)

**401 Unauthorized** = missing or invalid key. Keep keys secret; do not hard-code them in client-side code.

### Accounts and “Shared” Usage
- **Standard accounts** are self-serve via the console for API access and key management. Rate limits and billing are at the account/key level.
- **Enterprise** offerings target teams and high-volume users. They provide higher rate limits, SOC 2 Type II compliance, Zero Data Retention (ZDR – no training on your inputs/outputs), and the ability to discuss custom terms, VPC/on-prem options, BAAs, etc. Contact sales@typesafe.ai.[[6]](https://typesafe.ai/enterprise)

There is no published “shared account” tier. Technically, multiple people or services can use the same API key (one balance across all uses), but this is **not recommended**: it mixes billing, risks key exposure, causes rate-limit contention, and complicates debugging/auditing. Best practice is one key per project/service or proper team/enterprise setup with separate keys where supported. TypeSafe states they do not train on customer data and offers strong privacy controls for enterprise.

### Quick Recommendations
- Start with the official models page for the single source of truth on pricing + limits.
- Use the SDKs (they handle retries, connection pooling, and typed primitives).
- Batch questions aggressively to amortize the state cost.
- Monitor the `usage` field in responses and set up alerts for spend.
- For production/high scale, talk to sales early about enterprise limits and guarantees.

**Primary sources**: Official docs at https://docs.typesafe.ai/models (pricing, limits, context), https://docs.typesafe.ai/api (auth, errors, rate-limit handling), quickstart, and enterprise page. These were current as of October 2026; always verify live because limits are noted as dynamic.[[1]](https://docs.typesafe.ai/models)

For the absolute latest numbers or enterprise discussion, visit the console or email sales@typesafe.ai.

extra_sources.title: Models - TypeSafe AI
extra_sources.description:
## ​ Current models

| Jev 1.13 | `jev-1.13.0` |
 --- |
| Price (per Btok / per Mtok) | $42 / $0.042 |
| Rate limits | 100K tokens per second / 80 requests per second |
| Context length | 64k tokens per request; 32k tokens for `state` plus the longest question |
| Input | Text only. String, JSON object, or array of text values. No image, audio, or video input. | [...] Price: Charged per input token. Output tokens are free. A Btok is a billion tokens and an Mtok is a million tokens.
 Rate limits: Measured in tokens per second and requests per second. A request over either limit returns `429 Too Many Requests`. Our client SDKs retry with backoff by default and honor the `retry-after` header when the response carries one. If you call the HTTP API directly, see Handling rate limits.
 Context length: Jev ingests the `state` once and evaluates every question against it in parallel. The 64k budget covers the `state` plus all questions combined; the 32k budget applies to the `state` plus the single longest question. See Speculative fan-out for packing many questions into one request, and Jev 1.13 jaggedness for how accuracy shifts as the state grows. [...] ## ​ Data handling

Jev is not trained on customer requests or responses. See Legal for the Data Processing Agreement, the Privacy Policy, and details on zero data retention (ZDR) for enterprise customers.

## ​ Listing models

`GET /v1/models` returns the names your account can send in the `model` field, with a description and release date for each. It currently lists the aliases. Versioned IDs such as `jev-1.13.0` are accepted by the `model` field whether or not they appear in the list.

```
curl  \ curl   \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TYPESAFE_API_KEY" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TYPESAFE_API_KEY "
```
